chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray by the side of the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and even though the prayer of the believers reaches him, from wherever they may be.'
ai.seo_question: Does prayer by the Prophet's grave reach him if performed elsewhere?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia practice of praying near the Prophet’s grave (Salat al-Qabr) as a means of seeking intercession and spiritual connection. It underscores the concept of *tawassul* (seeking means of approach to God) through the Prophet, affirming that the spiritual merit of the believer's prayer reaches him regardless of physical distance, thereby validating the veneration of the grave as a locus of divine proximity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Send Salawaat by the side of the grave of the Prophetsaww, and even though the sending of the Salawaat by the Believers reaches himsaww, from wherever they may happen to be’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, has said, ‘Offer al-Salawat, next to the grave of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, although Salat of believers reach him wherever they may live. (The word al-Salat in this context may mean, ’Perform salat (prayer) as gift for the Holy Prophet,’ or say, ‘O Allah, grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause).”’
